affected_boundaries: host thread handoff to project resource retirement

observed_behavior: Successful handoff left the source checkout present and registered, created a destination thread, and switched the ordinary checkout to the worker branch.
expected_behavior: Retirement completes the original cleanup action without changing session identity or ordinary checkout state and verifies both path and Git registration are absent.
causal_mechanism: Coordinator policy inferred resource deletion and stable thread identity from an operation whose contract only transfers thread Git state.

anti_pattern.structural_description: An orchestration transition relies on side effects not guaranteed by the selected host capability.
anti_pattern.why_it_fails: The host can successfully perform the transfer while leaving the required deletion undone and changing unrelated ordinary-checkout state.

correct_pattern.required_invariant: Only the exact authenticated abandoned worktree may be retired, after its original session is archived and its accepted revision is integrated.
correct_pattern.implementation_description: Use the project's committed generation-fenced lifecycle adapter for the one authenticated claim; independently verify directory and Git registration absence before completing the original action.

applicability_conditions: Thread movement and resource retirement are distinct lifecycle operations.
known_non_matches: Attachment-scoped archival of a proven task-owned artifact remains a supported host operation.
confirmation_evidence: The coordinator reported successful handoff followed by an intact clean detached source checkout and a changed ordinary checkout.
regression_proofs: tests/campaign-orchestration.test.js: retirement fences the original archived session and reclaims only its authenticated worktree
